reviews.title: Okay for secondary monitor
reviews.comment: Bought 2 of these to put in portrait mode as side monitors just because I can. Color are dull and more washout than my other monitors. Spent hours messing around with OSD menu and found out the color calibration setting is not 1 to 1 even though they are the exact same monitor. As I set all the setting to the same value, each monitor produced different results. Especially the "Hue" setting as changing it to the same setting one monitor turned blue while the other turned yellow. Also, out of the box this monitor response time is not calibrated correctly, doing the UFO test, there a glow trailing behind which indicating an overshoot. Changing the overdrive  setting, all three option worsen rather than helping. Viewing angle is not good in portrait mode. There is a slight red hue shift when you are viewing off angle. I do believe it is an ips panel just a crappy one as it doesn't have black smearing issues like VA. Overall, not too bad for $140 ultrawide if buying it for secondary monitor like I am. But for gaming, look else where.
reviews.author: Prat S

reviews.title: Not a bad monitor but inaccurate description and some ghosting
reviews.comment: This monitor is not bad for the price, but the description is inaccurate. I bought this because it was supposed to have a glossy display, but in reality it is a matte display, not glossy, and the finish is fairly strong and quite noticeable on light backgrounds. In addition, I believe it is an IPS display, but the contrast is not 3000:1. IPS displays do not have a contrast that high unless it is IPS black, which this certainly is not. I also had a little bit of ghosting, especially in dark mode, which is common in displays at this price. The overdrive settings were not able to reduce it. On the plus side, I was able to get 165 HZ with the included DisplayPort cable using an M1 Pro MacBook Pro with a USB-C to DisplayPort adaptor.
